2.9.3 Implementation Aspect
For the BSW service component this pattern means that operations of the same service
interface might be called simultaneously on multiple partitions on the same- or even
different cores. One precondition therefore is that service APIs are specified to be
reentrant.
This attribute applies to single core- multi-threaded systems and allows
concurrent invocation of the operations by application SWCs on different tasks. If it is
not given (Reentrancy = Non Reentrant), it must not be overridden by this pattern by
allowing concurrent invocation of service interfaces by application SWCs on different
partitions.
Applying the pattern may also impact the runtime behavior of an API with respect to
its "Sync/Async" attribute. A return of an synchronous API does not necessarily mean
that the effect of the API has taken place but can also mean, that the API merely stored
the function arguments and has triggered an internal processing request related to the
API call. For example, the hypothetical API <MSN>_RequestState(x) is used to set
the module’s internal state to ’x’. If now the API is invoked on a different partition, it is
legit that <MSN> buffers ’x’ and performs the state change after the context has been
switched back.
